To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the next-to-next-to-leading-order (N2LO) Hamiltonian of NRQCD is derived and the complete matching of the N3LO Hamiltonian is performed including one- two- and three-loop contributions in the threshold expansion.
the next-to-next-to-leading-order Hamiltonian of potential NRQCD has been derived and that it is the most precise nonrelativistic Hamiltonian for bound states of heavy quarks to date.
we have derived and analyzed the N 3 LO Hamiltonian of potential NRQCD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the heavy quarkonium spectrum in the framework of nonrelativistic effective theories.
the calculation of the next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) contribution to the heavy-quark potential.
a new approach to nonperturbative QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the heavy-quark-antiquark bound state, the N 3 LO Hamiltonian is now fully known.
the N3LO NRQCD Hamiltonian has been derived, and that the complete N3LO spectrum for the heavy-quark system has been calculated.

, at NLO, NRQCD is not a good effective theory for heavy quarks, at NNLO, it is good for the heavy-quark mass, but not for the heavy-quonium spectrum, at NNNLO, it is not good for the heavy quark mass, but good for the heavy- quonium spectrum, and at N 4 LO it is good again for the heavy-quar mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N 3 LO Hamiltonian is derived in the full theory and in the static limit.
the N 3 LO corrections to the Hamiltonian and to the spectrum of the heavy-quarks are known.
the complete N 3 LO Hamiltonian of potential NRQCD is now available for all possible cases, including a nonvanishing QCD beta-function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic (NNLL) contribution is of the same order of magnitude as the N 2 LO contribution.
the N 3 LO spectrum of heavy-quarkonium can be calculated in a fully perturbative way.
the N 3 LO Hamiltonian is now known in full, and that it is now possible to perform a full N 4 LO computation of the heavy-quarks spectrum in QCD.
